scope: Expanded assertion-oracle review of three parent-selected color/transparency tests. This is not a full clause review and does not certify profile validity, all black-generation paths, every point of a spot curve, or all backends.

pdf_sources.bounded_rule: An ICCBased CMYK transparency-group space redefines DeviceCMYK within that group as the same blending space.
Output intent is one possible source of the page/output color condition; not recertified here.
/DefaultCMYK replaces DeviceCMYK when selected for an operation; not recertified here.

source.effective_errata: The inspected primary pages for §11.7.2 and this test's three routes have only navigation links, not an annotation modifying the tested redefinition/route rule. No sweeping errata census is claimed.
source.fixture_note: The test's custom v2 CMYK ICC profile is generated by test-local `cmyk_profile`/`cmyk_a2b_tag` from `press_xyz_of`; this pass does not certify every required ICC header field or complete-profile conformity.

assertion_and_consumer.actual: The test parses the same synthetic profile with `pdf_model::icc::Profile::parse`, computes `wanted = profile.to_rgb([0.5; 4])`, then checks raster pixels for three routing cases: page-group `/CS`, `/DefaultCMYK`, and output intent. A no-profile assumed-press control expects red 76–77 and must differ from the profile result by >8.
assertion_and_consumer.consumer: `interpret` builds the public model display list; `pixel` rasterizes through CPU. This exercises group/profile/default/output-intent routing to a visible result.
assertion_and_consumer.oracle_limit: The expected path uses the same ICC parser, transform, BPC and sRGB output implementation as the rendered path. Thus the test is a strong route-equivalence/control test but not an independent ICC-color oracle. The sibling `a_presss_grid_is_the_profile_at_its_samples_and_near_it_between_them` also calls `Profile::to_rgb`, so it shares this limitation. Lower-level `pdf-colour/src/icc.rs::the_lookup_table_interpolates_in_the_connection_space` has a literal 188 midpoint control for a simpler XYZ LUT, but it does not independently anchor this CMYK profile's expected pixel.
assertion_and_consumer.draft: `drafts/press_routes_literal_oracle.rs` replaces only the dynamically computed expected triple with [169,149,147]. `drafts/derive_press_pixel.py` independently enumerates the fixture's quantized two-point 4D CLUT corners, averages at the midpoint, applies the selected compensating map from the all-ink local black (Y=.0576), then transforms D50 XYZ to the tree's sRGB display output. It does not call `Profile::parse`, `Profile::to_rgb`, or renderer helpers. This is an independent regression oracle for the selected profile/output policy, not an ISO-required device pixel. The profile-validity caveat remains.

ledger_and_decisions.ledger: §11.7.2 is implemented with profile-backed group route assertions; §14.11.5 and §8.6.5.6 are exercised by the three routes, but this test alone does not certify their complete source rules.

adrs.review: The profile-backed blending-space choice is coherent with the ADR's decision to represent the document's named press as a sampled value. This fixture routes that value; the runtime-derived expected is not independent evidence for ICC conversion accuracy.
The assumed-press negative control makes the selected profile visibly distinct from the fallback. It is a route discriminator, not an independent absolute color oracle.

features.verdict: No source behavior failure established. Useful route integration test with shared numeric oracle; independent literal fixture oracle drafted for parent review.

pdf_sources.bounded_rule: For a DeviceRGB elementary object painted directly into a DeviceCMYK transparency group, use the current BG/UCR functions at painting.
RGB-to-CMYK equations: complementary C/M/Y, k=min(C,M,Y), BG(k) for K, UCR(k) removed from C/M/Y, and final range constraints.

source.effective_errata: EC3 issue #640 on physical 377 / printed 362 edits §10.4.2.2 and §10.4.2.3's variable spelling (`grey` to `gray`); its replacement retains the one-minus-gray term and does not change the §10.4.2.4 route exercised here. Primary page 450 has no annotation altering the tested §11.7.5.3 condition.

assertion_and_consumer.actual: The 1×1 inline DeviceRGB image contains bytes 0x33,0x66,0x99 = (0.2,0.4,0.6); with BG(k)=1-k and UCR(k)=k/2, source arithmetic yields CMYK (0.6,0.4,0.2,0.6). The test then computes its pixel expected value using `device_cmyk_blending_space().convert`.
assertion_and_consumer.consumer: The image sample is painted into a DeviceCMYK group and CPU rasterized. This exercises actual image sample decoding, current graphics-state pair application, group compositing, and output conversion.
assertion_and_consumer.oracle_limit: The final expected color shares the assumed DeviceCMYK-to-sRGB blending-space converter, so this assertion is not a standalone numeric oracle for that converter. However `crates/pdf-model/tests/black_generation_paint.rs::solid_selection_order_matches_image_and_clause_arithmetic` contains the same inline image sample and pair, and asserts literal pixel [52,62,79,255] alongside solid/stencil controls. That is a discriminating public image-path control independent of the runtime `convert` call.

ledger_and_decisions.ledger: §11.7.5.3 names the painting-time BG/UCR case; §10.4.2.4 is where the pair's arithmetic is defined. The broader row cites direct numeric `black_generation.rs` tests and render-path tests.

adrs.review: The use of explicit current BG/UCR for this DeviceRGB→DeviceCMYK group conversion is narrowly source-grounded. This image assertion complements solid/vector/forms tests; it is not evidence that BG/UCR controls every generic ICC conversion.
The selected pair here is explicitly supplied, so the separate ADR interpretation of a profile/default route is not invoked by this test.

features.verdict: Strong integration coverage; the selected assertion uses a shared final converter, but an existing exact-route literal pixel test independently anchors the same image sample and pair. No new test draft or behavior defect warranted.

pdf_sources.bounded_rule: Step b converts each separation to flat XYZ over an all-white matte; step c multiplies the separate results.
Continuation: the simulation output and process separations; this review is limited to the curve sample exercised by this test.
LogoGreen tint transform at full tint gives CMYK [0.84, 0, 0.44, 0.21]. Exact source locator not independently transcribed in this shard.

source.effective_errata: Physical pages 400–401 show only links around the tested §10.8.3 text; no annotation was found modifying step b/c in this bounded primary-page check.

assertion_and_consumer.actual: `SpotColourants::readable` in `crates/pdf-model/src/colourants.rs` constructs 256 samples by calling `space.flat_ratio(values, compensating())` at tint i/255. The selected test requires flat length 256, first sample approximately [1,1,1], then compares the final sample to `ColourSpace::Cmyk.flat_ratio([0.84,0,0.44,0.21], ...)`.
assertion_and_consumer.oracle_limit: The last-sample expected conversion calls the same flat_ratio function used to construct the table, so it does not independently validate CMYK flat-XYZ conversion. It does use a literal source-derived tint-transform result and is useful as a builder/tint-path assertion, but the numeric converter half is shared.
assertion_and_consumer.independent_sibling_anchor: `crates/pdf-model/tests/spot_press.rs` checks complete public separation-simulation pixels against handwritten arithmetic from LogoGreen's source tint transform and the explicitly selected process-device assumptions: `a_spot_alone_is_its_separations_colour` at tint .5 expects [134,198,183]; overprint tests at tint 1 expect [69,139,0] with process yellow and [2,13,11] with process black; RGB/ICC/Gray group tests repeat literal spot outputs. These are independent end-to-end expected values and cover interior and endpoint tints, although they do not test every one of 256 stored entries individually.
assertion_and_consumer.consumer: The `SpotColourant::flat()` curve is handed to pdf-render's separation compositor and is consumed by CPU/raster rendering. The sibling `spot_press.rs` exercises this public route rather than inspecting only the helper's intermediate vector.

ledger_and_decisions.ledger: §10.8.3 implemented status is tied to the requested simulation and step b/c paths. Existing `spot_press` literal pixels are stronger evidence for the visible selected tints than the self-comparison alone. The historical ledger note about ColorantTable/SHOULD has a separate parent-reviewed qualification and is not re-opened here.

adrs.review: The simulation algorithm and user-requested control have independent numeric product/white-matte assertions. This selected curve test alone does not prove the flat-XYZ arithmetic; spot_press supplies separate literals for the actually rendered consumer.

Spot colourants are represented as planes/curves and consumed in the renderer. Public `spot_press` assertions independently pin selected tint behavior, so no new full-table assertion was shown necessary by this bounded review.

features.verdict: The selected endpoint assertion has a shared conversion oracle, but existing public literal output tests cover both a mid tint and full-tint composites through the actual separated consumer. This pass does not identify an uncovered source requirement or justify a duplicate test.

unreviewed: No exhaustive audit of all ICC profile header requirements, all color intents, every BG/UCR path, or every tint sample of every spot curve.
No test was run in this shard; the press literal replacement is a scratch draft for parent integration/review only.
No claim that RGB/CMYK screen pixel values are uniquely mandated by ISO where the selected device-conversion algorithm is a processor choice.
